title: Proving who you are, again
category_name: Administrative burden: forms, queues, renewals, the time tax
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Every institution verifies you separately, none of them trust each other's verification, and each wants a different combination of documents you must locate, copy and produce in person.

title: The renewal treadmill
category_name: Administrative burden: forms, queues, renewals, the time tax
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Passport, licence, registration, insurance, membership, subscription, permit. Each has its own cycle and its own portal, so something is always about to lapse and the lapse is always your fault.

title: Open when you are at work
category_name: Administrative burden: forms, queues, renewals, the time tax
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Offices, clinics, banks and tradespeople operate during working hours, so accessing them costs annual leave or lost pay.

title: Hold music, and the person who cannot help you
category_name: Administrative burden: forms, queues, renewals, the time tax
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Support lines are built around cost per call. The person who answers can read the screen and rarely change what is on it.

title: The typo that becomes official
category_name: Errors: yours, theirs, and the ones nobody catches
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: One wrong character in a name, date, address or account number propagates into every system downstream, and correcting it is always harder than making it.

title: Their mistake, your problem
category_name: Errors: yours, theirs, and the ones nobody catches
imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
summary: Institutions presume their own records are correct. When they are not, discovering it, proving it and fixing it is entirely the work of the person harmed.

title: Mistaken for someone else
category_name: Errors: yours, theirs, and the ones nobody catches
imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
summary: Matching is fuzzy. A similar name, a shared birth date or a recycled phone number attaches another person's record - debts, fines, medical history - to you, and disproving it is your job.

title: After the crash
category_name: Accidents and physical injury
applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
scope_note: Anyone who drives or is driven. Includes crashes you caused.
summary: The collision takes four seconds. What follows is months of insurers, assessors, hire cars, medical appointments and an argument about liability you did not want to have.

title: The ordinary injury
category_name: Accidents and physical injury
imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
summary: A fall, a ladder, a kitchen, a football pitch, ice. The healing is the easy part; the hard part is doing your job and your life at reduced capacity while nobody adjusts anything.

title: You get ill, and nobody decided it
category_name: Illness and injury that simply arrives
imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
summary: Cancer, autoimmune disease, a cardiac event, a neurological condition. No behaviour reliably prevents them, no one is responsible, and the diagnosis reorganises everything around it.

title: The waiting list
category_name: Illness and injury that simply arrives
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Where care is rationed by queue rather than price, the wait is assigned to you without negotiation and without a date you can plan around.

title: The illness generates an invoice
category_name: Being billed for it: the health payment system you were born into
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: In systems that bill individuals, a medical event produces a bill nobody quoted in advance, for an amount nobody can state beforehand, from providers you did not choose.

title: Cover attached to a job
category_name: Being billed for it: the health payment system you were born into
applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
scope_note: Anyone whose health cover runs through employment.
summary: Where health cover comes through an employer, losing or changing work removes medical care at the same moment it removes income - and staying in a bad job becomes a medical decision.

title: The body slows on a timetable you do not set
category_name: The body's own schedule
imposed_by_note: The body and its schedule - ageing, injury, decline
summary: Recovery lengthens, sleep degrades, eyesight goes, strength declines. Gradual enough to be invisible, cumulative enough to be decisive, entirely non-negotiable.

title: Being burgled or robbed
category_name: Crime and other people's deliberate acts
applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
summary: Someone decides to take your things. The loss is the smallest part; the aftermath is locksmiths, insurers, reference numbers, and not feeling right in your own rooms.

title: On the receiving end of someone else's driving
category_name: Crime and other people's deliberate acts
applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
scope_note: Anyone on a road, including on foot or a bike.
summary: Another person's speed, phone or inattention arrives in your life at a junction, and everything that follows is yours to administer.

title: Where you live decides which disaster you get
category_name: Weather, disaster and where you happen to live
imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
summary: Flood, wildfire, hurricane, earthquake, heatwave, freeze. The exposure comes with the ground, and the ground came with the job, the family or the price.

title: Someone is trying to defraud you, professionally
category_name: Fraud, scams and identity theft
imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
summary: Calls, texts, emails and messages engineered by people who do this full time, arriving whether or not you engage with anything.

title: Your data was lost by someone you never dealt with
category_name: Fraud, scams and identity theft
imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
summary: Organisations you have no relationship with hold records about you and lose them. Nothing you did caused it and nothing you can do fixes it.

title: The job ends because someone else did arithmetic
category_name: Work, layoffs and career risk
applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Layoffs, restructures, acquisitions and closures arrive on a timetable set elsewhere. The decision is about headcount and cost centres, not about you, and the income stops anyway.

title: The manager you were assigned
category_name: Work, layoffs and career risk
applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
summary: Whether a job is tolerable is largely one person, allocated to you, who can change without notice and without any change to your contract.

title: Working while ill, because the alternative is worse
category_name: Work, layoffs and career risk
applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Where sick pay is thin or absent, illness becomes a financial calculation, and the calculation usually says go in.

title: Your largest expense is set annually by someone else
category_name: Housing, rent and the things that break
applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: For renters, the price of having somewhere to live is decided by another party once a year, and the only counter-move costs more than accepting it.

title: Things break, and they break together
category_name: Housing, rent and the things that break
applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
summary: Boiler, roof, car, washing machine, phone. Each has a lifespan, they were often bought at the same time, and they fail at whatever moment they fail at.

title: Someone will need looking after
category_name: Family, care and bereavement
applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
summary: An ageing parent, a sick partner, a child with additional needs. It arrives unscheduled, lasts years, is unpaid, and lands on whoever is nearest or least able to refuse.

title: Bereavement, and the paperwork of it
category_name: Family, care and bereavement
imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
summary: Grief arrives with an administrative workload - registration, probate, accounts, utilities, pensions - executed by the person least able to concentrate.

title: Locked out of your own account
category_name: Technology, data and digital dependency
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Identity online is a chain of recovery methods. Break one link - a dead number, a lost authenticator, a closed email - and the chain does not reconnect.

title: The thing you relied on is discontinued
category_name: Technology, data and digital dependency
imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
summary: Services close, formats are abandoned, apps are bought and shut, devices stop receiving updates. The decision is a company's; the migration is yours.

title: You must have a car, because of how the place was built
category_name: Transport and getting places
applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Where there is no viable transit, car ownership is not a preference - it is a condition of employment, imposed by planning decisions made before you arrived.

title: The commute
category_name: Transport and getting places
applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: A daily journey is the largest recurring involuntary time cost most working people carry. It is unpaid, not counted as work, and mostly set by where housing is affordable.

title: The credential you must hold to be considered
category_name: Credentials you must hold to be considered
applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Employers set entry requirements. Roles that once needed a school certificate now need a degree, without a corresponding change in the work - so the qualification is a toll, not a choice.

title: The structures that made friends are removed
category_name: Social life, friendship and loneliness
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: School, university and early jobs supply repeated unplanned contact. Adult life does not, so friendship becomes something that must be organised or it ends.

title: You cannot afford to enforce your own rights
category_name: Legal, contracts and disputes
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Most everyday legal wrongs are worth less than the cost of pursuing them, so the right exists and the remedy does not - and the other party knows it.

title: Compelled participation
category_name: Legal, contracts and disputes
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Jury service, tax filing, census, registration, court witness summons. Duties that take real time, are not optional, and are scheduled by the state.

title: Everything you have requires upkeep
category_name: Maintenance, queues and entropy
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Possessions, accounts, documents, health and qualifications all decay without input. The work returns you to baseline; none of it is progress.

title: The queue
category_name: Maintenance, queues and entropy
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Waiting is allocated to you by whoever is providing the thing, in units they do not pay for and you cannot spend elsewhere.

title: You were born into a cohort and the cohort has a price
category_name: Luck, timing and the cohort you were born into
imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
summary: House prices, interest rates, the labour market in your graduation year, whether a pandemic falls in your twenties. None is chosen, and all of it compounds.

title: The volume of small compulsory decisions
category_name: Psychological load and what it costs downstream
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: Tariffs, plans, policies, renewals and options all require comparison. The choosing is imposed; the alternative is paying the default price.

title: Ambient activation that never resolves
category_name: Psychological load and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
summary: News, notifications and always-on messaging produce a baseline of alertness nobody opted into, and it does not switch off because the devices do not.
